🎙
Remarks
by Russian MFA Ambassador-at-Large
Rodion Miroshnik
during the dialogue with Chair of the UN Committee against Torture Claude Heller
(New York, October 15, 2026)
Read in full
Broadcast of the entire meeting
💬
The UN’s excessively permissive attitude towards the existence of
an entire network of “secret prisons”
for POWs in Kiev-controlled territory
encourages the spread of this criminal practice
and disregard for the provisions of the relevant UN Convention.
Hundreds of Russian servicemen we have interviewed,
who endured the hell of Ukrainian prison camps
, consistently describe a
n entire network of facilities holding POWs
. Several reports by foreign human rights defenders refer to them in highly evasive terms as
“transit prisons”
, where servicemen are held during the initial stages of captivity.
In these cramped stone cells, underground dungeons and cages, generally located on the premises of Ukrainian military units and nationalist battalions,
everything human is subjected to utter degradation – from personal dignity to life itself.
Militants who conceal their faces behind masks and balaclavas and address one another by call signs
subject captured Russian servicemen to inhuman abuse.
❗️
Simulated drowning, “electric chairs”, dog attacks and amputations without anaesthesia are just a fraction of the methods systematically employed there by Ukrainian punitive forces.
***
The Kiev authorities deny human rights defenders and observers access to these
torture chambers
. Yet we have collected
hundreds of accounts
of what happens there and have repeatedly submitted them to the UN Secretariat. I am certain that conscientious, impartial human rights defenders could obtain this information with even a minimal willingness to do so.
We know for a fact that such
“prisons”
exist in the
Kharkov, Dnepropetrovsk and Sumy regions
, and even
in Kiev
.
In this connection,
I have just one question
: what will it take for the UN Committee against Torture to make it a priority to investigate Ukraine’s well-known yet persistently ignored system of
“secret prisons”
?
Many experts are aware of this shameful phenomenon.
What is lacking is the political will to overcome pressure from foreign parties complicit in the conflict
, who shield the Kiev regime from accountability and detailed investigations into its actions.
👉
I hope the Committee will take these remarks into account and finally address this unacceptable practice in order to put an end to it once and for all.
#KievRegimeCrimes

🎙
Statement
by Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov at the Plenary Session of the
#CSTO
,
#CIS
and
#SCO
Conference on Security in Central Asia and Afghanistan
(
Moscow, October 16, 2026
)
💬
Sergey Lavrov:
Everyone has an interest in ensuring that
Central Asia remains a region of peace & prosperity
, underpinned by broad, mutually beneficial cooperation among all the states in the region and, of course, their immediate neighbours.
For Russia, this region holds particular strategic significance
: geographical, historical and humanitarian factors mean that important Russian interests are concentrated here.
☝️
We see one way of safeguarding these interests in
maintaining relations of alliance and strategic partnership on an equal footing with all Central Asian countries,
helping them ensure
peaceful and secure development
both bilaterally and through the integration mechanisms operating in the region.
We assess the situation in Central Asia as stable and conducive to international cooperation
, despite the well-known risks. We appreciate
the enormous contribution
made by the region’s Leaders to creating all the necessary conditions for this.
At the same time,
we must not lose sight of the risks we all know about
, which arise primarily from the actions of certain external players seeking to pursue their narrow, self-serving geopolitical objectives without regard for the region’s specific circumstances or the interests of the friendly peoples of Central Asia.
Today, especially before this audience, there is no need to convince anyone that
the countries of the “collective West” have been trying for many years to create flashpoints along our borders
. In particular, their role in
deliberately engineering the Ukrainian crisis
is well known – through years of
relentless eastward NATO expansion towards Russia’s borders
, as well as through unqualified support for the openly neo-Nazi, Russophobic Kiev regime, which is once again showing its true colours in these very days.
❗️
In this connection,
I would emphasise that
absolutely any country in the world
, including our partners in Central Asia,
could fall victim to the West’s geopolitical expansion and the “colour revolutions” it orchestrates.
Such attempts have already been made against a number of our neighbours, but were successfully thwarted.
***
Developments in Afghanistan could still adversely affect regional security
, especially if unscrupulous external players exploit them for short-term interests that have nothing in common with those of Central Asian countries and Russia.
We strive to be realistic and, in this regard, understand that overcoming
the grim legacy
left by the US and other NATO countries after two decades of inglorious occupation of Afghanistan will take a long time.
👉
We proceed from the understanding that the Taliban government is a reality that must be reckoned with.
A growing number of countries are coming to recognise this. On the political front, we are working to consolidate external support for the authorities in Kabul and those aspects of their work that objectively serve the interests of regional security.
Russia fully shares the vision of Afghanistan as an independent, united and peaceful state, free from war and drugs.
We regard as an important success the fact that
the latest meeting of the Moscow Format Consultations on Afghanistan
, held in Moscow in early October, reaffirmed the participating countries’ rejection of a confrontational approach towards Kabul.

item.title: 🗓 On October 15, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov took part in the 7th Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia
item.description: 🗓 On October 15, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov took part in the 7th Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia ( #CICA ) in Baku. 👉 Sergey Lavrov's opening remarks at the Summit's Plenary Session Discussions focused on prospects for CICA’s development and its adaptation to the changing international environment. The Russian Side emphasised the importance of integrating CICA harmoniously into the emerging architecture of cooperation across Eurasia , with a view to establishing a continent-wide framework of equal and indivisible security and seamless cross-border socioeconomic connectivity. 🤝 Sergey Lavrov reaffirmed Russia’s unwavering commitment to deepening practical cooperation within CICA , including in the areas it coordinates : international information security and support for small and medium-sized enterprises. Other priorities include fostering contacts between volunteer organisations and advancing mechanisms for practical industrial cooperation. Our country’s contribution to strengthening transport and logistics links across the CICA region was also highlighted. Russia welcomed the extension of Azerbaijan’s CICA chairmanship for 2027-2028 and supported Laos joining the Conference as a full member.

item.title: 🇺🇳 On October 16, 1945, the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
item.description: 🇺🇳 On October 16, 1945, the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations ( #FAO ) was established – a UN specialised agency leading international efforts to combat hunger. The Organisation was officially founded at its first Conference in Quebec. Since 1951, FAO headquarters have been located in Rome. On April 11, 2006, Russia ratified the FAO Constitution and became a full member of this UN specialised agency. 🌐 At present, the Organisation comprises 193 member states , one member organisation (the European Union) and two associate members – the Faroe Islands and Tokelau. The Organisation’s work is focused on eradicating hunger and tackling food security and malnutrition. The FAO is geared towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), above all SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 2 (Zero Hunger) and SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities), and also contributes to the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development through a transition to more efficient, inclusive, resilient and sustainable agri-food systems. 🇷🇺 Russia remains a responsible and constructive partner of the FAO. Projects funded by our country through the Organisation are aimed at strengthening the agro-industrial capacity of partner countries and addressing their pressing socioeconomic challenges.

🎙
Remarks
by Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov at the Plenary Session of
the 7th Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia
(Baku, October 15, 2026)
💬
Sergey Lavrov:
Over the past four years, challenging as this period has been, first
Astana
and then
Baku
, at the helm of
the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia
(
#CICA
), have made
notable progress
in strengthening our regional platform.
New mechanisms have been established
: a financial summit, a women’s council and a partnership network of leading universities.
The Secretariat has been significantly strengthened
, including through broader geographical representation among its staff.
CICA’s voice is increasingly heard at multilateral events
. Growing interest in its activities attests to its appeal.
🇱🇦
In this regard, we congratulate Laos on joining the Conference.
The system of international relations is undergoing fundamental changes.
A new, fairer
#MultipolarWorld
order is taking shape before our eyes.
Against this backdrop, a clear message is emerging from Greater Eurasia
: countries need to advance together, ensuring equal and indivisible security for all, whereby no State’s security can be ensured at the expense of the security of others. This philosophy is clearly reflected in the final declaration to be adopted at the conclusion of our meeting.
This shared outlook drives our efforts to create
a stable and predictable political and economic environment across the Eurasian continent
, conducive to deeper, mutually beneficial practical cooperation.
👉
We invite our partners to join us in drafting
a political document on diversity and multipolarity in the 21st century
that would apply across Eurasia
.
We
discussed
this initiative with many of the countries represented here on the sidelines of
the high-level week
of
the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly in New York
. We will continue these discussions at
the Fourth Conference on Eurasian Security
, to be held in Minsk in early November.
***
We are convinced that
CICA’s transformation towards a pan-Eurasian outlook
, in keeping with the times,
is a natural path for our association
, dictated by objective realities.
Many participating countries are Eurasian in character
, and some geographically as well. Our shared task is
to adapt the Conference to new realities
and
harness its potential to promote growth and prosperity
across the continent.
Today, the constructive atmosphere within our platform stems from
a shared commitment to broad, pragmatic cooperation
.
☝️
Not least because of its membership,
CICA is unencumbered by contrived political constructs such as the “rules-based order” or bloc-based approaches
designed to serve the interests and convenience of insiders alone.

item.description: ⚡️ Federal Security Service of the Russian Federation : The Federal Security Service of the Russian Federation ( #FSB ) has detained a Swedish national in the Sebezh District of the Pskov Region after he illegally crossed the Russian Federation’s State border from a neighbouring country. It has been established that, between February and June 2026, the foreign national served under contract in an organisation designated as terrorist in the Russian Federation , commanding an unmanned aircraft systems squad in the 24th Separate assault battalion. ❗️ There is documentary evidence confirming his participation in hostilities against our country as a member of the Ukrainian armed forces. Under the guise of joining the Russian Armed Forces , he was travelling to the Russian Federation to carry out acts of sabotage and terrorism against military facilities. Criminal proceedings have been initiated against the foreign national under Part 1 of Article 322 of the Russian Criminal Code (Illegal Crossing of the State Border of the Russian Federation). The initiation of further criminal proceedings under Article 205.5 (Organising the Activities of a Terrorist Organisation and Participating in Its Activities) and Article 359 (Mercenary Activities) of the Russian Criminal Code is under consideration .

#AEW2026
Russian Ambassador Roman Ambarov Addresses African Energy Week in Cape Town
🎙
On 15 October, Russian Ambassador to South Africa and Lesotho
Roman Ambarov
delivered a speech at the Russian-African session of
African Energy Week 2026
, taking place in Cape Town from 12 to 16 October.
🔹
Energy security and industrial development
The Ambassador emphasised that reliable and affordable energy is the foundation of industrial development, economic sovereignty and job creation across Africa.
“Energy cooperation must be practical, long-term and mutually beneficial. It should not end with the sale of equipment or the delivery of fuel. It should include technologies, engineering expertise, localisation, education and the training of national specialists.”
🔹
Nuclear energy: a strategic area for cooperation
Ambassador Ambarov highlighted the role of nuclear power in providing reliable baseload electricity with very low carbon emissions. Against the backdrop of South Africa’s plans to develop
5,200 MW of new nuclear capacity by 2039
, he reaffirmed Russia’s readiness for professional dialogue and cooperation in this field.
A nuclear project is not simply a power station. It is a long-term industrial and educational partnership that can support universities, engineering companies, construction firms, manufacturers and research institutions for decades.”
As a major example of Russian–African nuclear cooperation, the Ambassador pointed to the
El Dabaa Nuclear Power Plant in Egypt
, where Rosatom is constructing four nuclear units with a combined capacity of
4,800 MW
. The project encompasses not only construction, but also nuclear fuel supply, operational support and the training of Egyptian specialists.
🔹
Practical solutions for South Africa’s energy needs
Other areas identified for potential cooperation include:
▪️
LNG and petroleum supplies;
▪️
modernisation and improved efficiency of coal-fired power stations;
▪️
expansion and modernisation of electricity transmission networks;
▪️
offshore oil and gas exploration;
▪️
advanced power engineering technologies and equipment.
The Ambassador also stressed the importance of
technology transfer, localisation and cooperation with South African companies
to ensure that energy partnerships deliver lasting benefits for the local economy.
“The task is not to choose one technology for ideological reasons. The task is to build a system that works.”
🤝
Russia stands ready to work with South Africa and other African countries on energy solutions that reflect their national priorities, strengthen energy security and support sustainable industrial development.
